case_title: Suraj Jagannath Jadha v. State of Maharashtra
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 (conviction); s.300 fourthly considered; Exception 4 to s.300 and s.304 Part II considered as alternative
weapon: Kerosene poured as accelerant and a lit match-stick; no weapon mentioned
evidence_type: Dying declaration (recording conversation between victim and accused); no other evidence discussed in the judgment
aggravating_circumstances: Victim set ablaze while trying to run away; accused fully conscious of consequences; no provocation; no proven inebriation
mitigating_circumstances: None noted by the court; defence alleged intoxication and that accused poured water to save victim, both rejected
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC; sentence not stated in judgment
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction under s.302 IPC confirmed
neutral_facts: The victim was the accused's wife. According to the prosecution's account, after abusing and assaulting the victim, the accused poured kerosene on her person and set her ablaze. The victim was trying to run out of the house to save herself and was attempting to open the latch of the door when the accused, coming from behind, threw a lit match-stick on her and set her on fire. The incident is recorded in a dying declaration by the victim, which describes a conversation between the victim and the accused at the time. According to that declaration, after the victim came out of the room making noise, the accused poured water on her. The defence said the accused was under the influence of liquor at the time, that he poured water to try to save the victim, and that he was himself injured in the process. The State submitted that the victim was pregnant, about 18 to 20 weeks, at the time. The victim died from burns.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from burns after being set ablaze with kerosene
number_of_offences: 1 charged (s.302 IPC as stated); 1 finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Not found as premeditation; court held the act was conscious and deliberate, and that its spur-of-the-moment nature does not reduce culpability (adopting Santosh)
motive: Not identified (State's submission describes abuse and assault before the act; no motive found)
key_evidence_accepted: Dying declaration, especially the account of the conversation between victim and accused, relied on to find the accused was conscious
post_offence_conduct: Accused poured water only after the victim screamed for help; treated as an attempt to cloak guilt and not mitigating (quoting Santosh, applied by the Court)
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 09.10.2018; Supreme Court: 13.12.2019
legal_representation: Appellant: Sushil Karanjkar, Nikhilesh Kumar, K. N. Rai. State: Nishant Ramakantrao Katneshwarkar, Anoop Kandari
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302 IPC; High Court (Criminal Appeal No. 723 of 2013): appeal dismissed, conviction confirmed; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Kalu Ram distinguished as accused not highly inebriated; pouring kerosene and lighting match are intimately connected; s.300 fourthly applies; later water-pouring was an attempt to cloak guilt; victim was pregnant
defence_argument: No intention to kill; accused intoxicated; poured water to save victim and was injured; Kalu Ram applies so conviction should be altered to s.304 Part II
legal_principle_applied: Intoxication is not a defence unless it renders accused incapable of forming intention; s.300 fourthly applies to act imminently dangerous to cause death; Exception 4 not applicable absent evidence of high inebriation; later water-pouring not mitigating
precedent_relied_upon: Santosh v. State of Maharashtra (2015) 7 SCC 641 (relied on); Bhagwan Tukaram Dange v. State of Maharashtra (2014) 4 SCC 270 (relied on); Kalu Ram v. State of Rajasthan (2000) 10 SCC 324 (distinguished)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Accused fully conscious of consequences; act done while victim was trying to escape; no proven high inebriation
